heldout_model.name: claude-haiku
heldout_model.reason: Gemini now needs a $50 minimum prepay, so gemini-flash is not used.
heldout_model.rule: Held out from the failure map, thresholds and all tuning. It runs only once, in the final --final evaluation (AGENTS.md section 8). No claude-haiku rows were collected on the real banks before this decision.

asurre.selection_rule: Hold out the source with the smallest total respondent count; break ties by the most recent survey year.
asurre.provenance: Counts are copied from the version-controlled ASURRE source configs under data/raw/asurre/configs. The decision was made before fitting or inspecting model outcomes.

gss.selection_rule: Use categorical core questions with 2-4 substantive choices and at least 500 usable responses, spanning wellbeing, interpersonal trust, and institutional confidence; exclude demographics and political or religious identity.
gss.ingestion_requirement: Copy exact wording, value codes, missing-value codes, release identifier, and checksum from the official NORC export into the GSS loader manifest before building the bank.

pilot_folds.low_effort_ids: pilot_data/low_effort_ids.txt (full session_ids; any id not among the pilot sessions is an error)
pilot_folds.rule: One session-to-fold assignment for every pilot analysis: the router's cross-fitting (scripts/run_real_router.py) and the behaviour-threshold calibration (scripts/calibrate_behaviour.py). Folds are assigned on all pilot sessions before any exclusion; low-effort sessions are dealt across the folds first. Change k or seed only here and in adr/replay/folds.py together, never per run.

style_profile.used_for: AI style rows of the v1 survey-bank runs (scripts/run_survey_banks.py rescore)
style_profile.check_against_handoff: Same numbers as Archana's processed/style_profile.json in ADR-runs-handoff-2026-11-17.zip (file sha256 297203e7...0ed88e4): feature means, feature stds, mid/high thresholds, n_training, sources, raw/config sha256s and per-question response counts are all identical. The files differ only in the paths they record (Windows vs macOS) and decisions_sha256.
style_profile.hashes: file_sha256 is the regenerated file as written. profile_sha256 is sha256 of the 'profile' object as compact JSON with sorted keys; it ignores paths, so it is the same for both files. The file's own decisions_sha256 refers to this file before this entry was added, so regenerating now gives a new file_sha256 but the same profile_sha256.

router_calibration.evidence_bounds: each mechanism's running total is bounded to [neg_floor_frac * B, mech_cap_frac * A]: one check alone cannot pause a session; it can clear one (cleared = no evidence of AI found)

wald.formula: A = ln((1 - beta) / alpha), B = ln(beta / (1 - alpha)); the cap and floor are fractions of these nominal values

router_calibration.threshold_rule: The review threshold is calibrated on honest sessions by session-level cross-fitting (adr/replay/crossfit.py, folds from adr/replay/folds.py): every honest session is scored with a failure map that never saw it, and resampled honest sessions are drawn per fold from that fold's sessions only. A_0.05 (headline) and A_0.01 (secondary) are the smallest thresholds that pause at most 5% / 1% of the resampled honest sessions; A_max (lowest threshold pausing none of the real sessions) is also reported. 95% CIs bootstrap over sessions.

ablations.no_cap: mech_cap_frac None: a single check may pause a session
ablations.twocheck: neg_floor_frac 0.65: no single check may clear a session

evidence.ai_sessions: 120 composite gpt-mini sessions: L0, L2, L2g x copy_paste, doc_upload, 20 each

router_calibration.rule: run_real_router.py's defaults must match this entry (tests/test_router_calibration.py). Change it only by a team decision, never per run.
